explorer.headline: Fly a spacecraft through the solar system
explorer.sub: Select a destination. The application finds the launch date and calculates the flight.
explorer.live: The solar system at this time: {date}

target.distance: Distance from the Earth at this time

famous.note: The application calculates this flight from the launch date and the flyby dates of the actual mission. The Expert mode shows the differences between this flight and the actual flight.

story.voyager2: Voyager 2 did a flyby of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. The gravity of each planet sent the spacecraft to the next planet.
story.cassini: Cassini did two flybys of Venus, then a flyby of the Earth and a flyby of Jupiter. Each flyby gave it more speed. It then went into orbit around Saturn.
story.newhorizons: New Horizons got more speed from the gravity of Jupiter. It then did a flyby of Pluto.
story.voyager1: Voyager 1 did a flyby of Jupiter and a flyby of Saturn. At Saturn it flew near the moon Titan. Then it went out of the plane of the planets.
story.mars2020: Mars 2020 flew to Mars with no flyby. It went into the atmosphere with the rover Perseverance.
story.juno: Juno flew around the Sun one time. It then did a flyby of the Earth to get more speed and went into orbit around Jupiter.
story.ulysses: Ulysses used the gravity of Jupiter to go out of the plane of the planets. It then flew above the poles of the Sun.
story.pioneer11: Pioneer 11 did a flyby of Jupiter and then flew across the solar system to Saturn. It was the first spacecraft at Saturn.
